In August 2026, the Company announced the strategic divestiture of its European operations which is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2027, and the intended closure of its European fiber cement business.

Other income, net increased due to a $19.4 million non-cash gain on the foreign currency forward contracts entered into to hedge our exposure to fluctuations in exchange rates associated with the anticipated Euro-denominated proceeds from the sale of our Fermacell business.

Because of these limitations, none of these metrics should be considered indicative of discretionary cash available to us to invest in the growth of our business or as measures of cash that will be available to us to meet our obligations.

During the first half of calendar year 2027 we expect to receive approximately $980.0 million (as of the date of the announcement), of cash proceeds related to the sale of our Fermacell business, subject to customary adjustments for net debt and working capital as of closing.

Management expects these proceeds to further enhance the Company's liquidity position and expects to apply approximately $600.0 million of the proceeds toward debt repayment, with the remainder available for general corporate purposes, including share repurchases and working capital needs.

Based on our existing cash balances, together with anticipated operating cash flows and unutilized credit facilities, we anticipate we will have sufficient funds to meet our planned working capital and other expected cash requirements for the next twelve months.
During fiscal year 2027, we will contribute A$128.2 million to AICF, excluding interest, in quarterly installments.

statements.t: Aaron Erter, CEO of James Hardie, said, "We delivered a strong second quarter, with sales from continuing operations up 24%, well above the market and at the high end of our guidance range.
Our synergy momentum continues to build, with commercial synergies on track to reach our fiscal 2027 target and cost synergies ahead of schedule.

Based on our broad set of self-help growth levers and our confidence in continuing to outperform the market, we are reaffirming our consolidated fiscal 2027 sales and Adjusted EBITDA outlook and raising our free cash flow target."
We are reaffirming our consolidated full-year fiscal 2027 net sales and Adjusted EBITDA guidance and increasing our free cash flow target to more than $650 million.
We expect Adjusted EBITDA to be lower in the third quarter and second half driven by DR&A seasonality in Q3, incremental freight costs and the weaker macro environment.
Together with the expected proceeds from the Europe divestiture, we remain on track to reach net leverage below 2.0x by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2028."

We provide certain elements of our outlook on a non-GAAP basis, as we cannot predict some elements that are included in reported GAAP results, including the impact of actuarial estimates on asbestos-related assets and liabilities in future periods.
We expect to apply approximately $600 million of proceeds from the Europe divestiture, which is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2027, toward debt repayment.
Together with continued free cash flow generation, this is expected to support our target of net leverage below 2.0x by the end of the second quarter of FY2028.

For FY2027, we continue to expect capital expenditures to be in the range of approximately 6% to 7% of net sales, reflecting maintenance and targeted growth investments across the manufacturing network.
Our footprint today is well positioned and equipped to support demand across both fiber cement and decking, and we do not anticipate the need for significant new capacity in the near term.

The previously announced closures of our Fontana, California and Summerville, South Carolina facilities are expected to generate approximately $25 million in annualized cost savings for Fiscal Year 2027.
